entries.title: Workgroup chat: links to single messages, and notes sent by email
entries.summary: Each workgroup chat message now has its own link. Opening it goes to the chat, finds the message (loading older messages if needed) and highlights it. Activity items for chat posts link to the message itself. Notes a reviewer sent by email and that were posted for them show a 'via email' label, keep their formatting (paragraphs, lists, links), list any attached files with their size, and link the reviewer's name to their Canopi profile when we can find it.
changes: Chat messages have permalinks: /workgroups/<slug>?tab=chat&m=<message id>
Activity on /activity and the workgroup Activity tab links to the exact chat message when Gov Hub sends its id
Notes relayed by email show formatted text, a 'via email' label, attachments, and the author's Canopi profile link
Attachments download through the site, signed in, as members-only files
entries.verify: After Gov Hub returns message ids, open a chat message link from a DP's Activity tab: the chat opens on that message and highlights it. A relayed email note shows 'via email', its files and a profile link.
entries.intent: Reviewers who answered by email get their notes posted under their own name in the DP workgroup chat, and people can link straight to them.

entries.title: Review tab shows style-pass proposals; style tasks for workgroups
entries.summary: From 20 October each chapter gets one style-pass proposal holding all its mechanical style-guide fixes (Meta-Layer capitalization, dashes, the '(Non-Normative)' label, § references). The Review tab labels it 'style pass' and lists every line before and after, so co-editors approve or decline it once. Three new weekly tasks cover the judgement calls: making each MUST and SHOULD testable, adding sources, and deciding the style pass.
changes: Review tab: style-pass proposals show a summary and an expandable list of every line edit, labelled by rule
New tasks for 19 and 26 October: testable requirements, cite sources, co-editors decide the style pass
entries.verify: After the Gov Hub style-pass bundles are created, a DP's Review tab shows one 'style pass' item with 'Show all N line edits'.
entries.intent: Apply the agreed style guide to existing chapters without burying co-editors in hundreds of small proposals.

entries.title: Style guide for the Desirable Properties book
entries.summary: A new page, /style-guide, sets how the book is written so 23 chapters read as one: who we write for, voice, requirement language (MUST/SHOULD/MAY), chapter structure, headings, terms, formatting, cross-references, sources, how to write a patch or insert, and guidance for co-editors. Most rules record what the chapters already do; the rest settle where they disagree. The same rules are available as text for the upcoming AI check of patches and inserts.
changes: New /style-guide page: 11 sections, 49 rules, with do/don't examples drawn from the book
Rules derived from a count across all 23 live chapters (e.g. 115 capital MUST/SHOULD inside '(Non-Normative)' sections; Meta-Layer spelled two ways)
styleGuideAsText() exports the guide for AI review prompts
Linked from the About menu, /process, and the Review tab's decision note
entries.verify: Open /style-guide: eleven sections from 'Who we write for' to 'For co-editors'; About menu lists Style guide.
entries.intent: Consistent tone and style across chapters, agreed at the 12 Oct 2026 session; the basis for the AI pre-check of manual patches and inserts.

entries.title: Workgroup cards show co-editor staffing, not a 3-member target
entries.summary: Workgroup cards on /workgroups now read, for example, '2 members · co-editors 0 of 2' or '4 members · fully staffed', instead of 'needs 1 more for a working group'. The 3-member target is gone from the workgroups intro, Start Here and the workgroup Getting Started tab; the Co-editors section above the tabs covers staffing.
changes: DP cards: member count plus co-editor seats from the readiness data; amber until two co-editors, green when fully staffed
DP Discovery card: member count only (it has no co-editors)
Workgroups intro and Start Here: 'at least 3 people' replaced with the two-co-editor rule
Getting Started tab: member-target box removed
entries.verify: Open /workgroups: each DP card shows 'n members · co-editors x of 2' or 'fully staffed'; no card mentions 'more for a working group'.
entries.intent: Two co-editors, not a member count, is what makes a DP fully staffed.

entries.title: Becoming a co-editor is easy to find; '3 members' check removed
entries.summary: The Co-editors card now sits above the workgroup tabs and says plainly how many co-editors the DP needs, with a 'Become a co-editor' button, what the role involves, and why you can't take a seat when you can't. Workgroup cards on /workgroups link straight to it. The 'Workgroup has at least 3 members' readiness item is gone; two co-editors is what makes a DP fully staffed.
changes: Co-editors card moved from the bottom of the header to its own section above the tabs
'Claim a seat' renamed 'Become a co-editor', with what the role involves and a character countdown
Shows why a seat can't be taken (already a co-editor, seats taken, account under 7 days, per-person limit)
Co-editors see a link to the Review tab; 'Nominate them' for members
Header 'Nominate' is now 'Nominate coordinator'; /workgroups cards get 'Become a co-editor'
Readiness: 'at least 3 members' removed from the card, board and process page
entries.verify: Signed in, open a DP workgroup page: the Co-editors section is above the tabs with 'Become a co-editor'. Needs Gov Hub #16 (bearer-token seat routes).
entries.intent: Members must be able to see and take an open co-editor seat without hunting for it.

entries.title: Invite with Email: events and perspectives load again
entries.summary: On production the Invite with Email tab showed 'The string did not match the expected pattern' instead of the events and perspectives you can include. A one-off rename of the 'Fork in the Web' perspective ran on every request and, when both the old and new entries existed, broke the unique-name rule each time. The rename now runs only when it is safe, the list loads even if one part fails, and a failure shows a plain message saying the invitation can still be sent.
changes: Perspective rename runs on one row and only when the new name is free; first-run seed ignores duplicates
Rename and seed run once per server process instead of on every request
/api/invite-content returns whatever loaded and logs what failed, instead of a bare 500
Invite tab shows a readable message when the list cannot load, instead of Safari's JSON parse error
entries.verify: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://desirableproperties.org/api/invite-content returns 200, and the Invite with Email tab lists events and perspectives.
entries.intent: Inviting people to workgroups must not be blocked or confused by optional content failing to load.

entries.title: Co-editors: coordinator seat, claim or nominate; a no needs a reason
entries.summary: Each workgroup page now has a Co-editors card showing the DP's two seats. The coordinator holds one seat automatically; the other is claimed, or a member nominates someone who becomes co-editor the moment they accept. On the Review tab, Decline stays disabled until the co-editor writes a note the author can read. Two co-editors now mean a DP is fully staffed; the 3-member check is shown for context only.
changes: New Co-editors card on each workgroup page: seats, Claim a seat, Nominate a member, Revoke
Co-editor removed from the generic Nominate dropdown (coordinator nominations only)
Review tab: Approve / Decline with a decision note; Decline is disabled until the note has text, and the note is sent to Gov Hub
Readiness board: 'fully staffed' = both co-editor seats; member count no longer counts toward Ready
Process, workgroups, FAQ and role copy updated for the new seat rules and the agreed 7-day decision rule
entries.verify: On a DP workgroup page the Co-editors card shows 'n of 2'. On the Review tab, Decline is greyed out until text is typed in Decision note. Requires the matching Gov Hub release (feature/co-editor-nominations).
entries.intent: Implements the co-editor decisions from the 12 Oct 2026 DP session: coordinators are co-editors, seats are claimed or nominated (opt-in), and every rejection carries a rationale.

entries.title: Sign-in uses each site's own Web3Auth ID
entries.summary: The site no longer falls back to production's Web3Auth client ID. Production and staging each name their own ID, and if the ID is missing, sign-in shows a clear error instead of quietly using production's.
changes: Removed the hardcoded production client ID from the Web3Auth config and token check
Production and staging pm2 configs each set their own WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID_DEVNET
A missing ID now returns a clear error on sign-in; other pages still load
entries.verify: Open sign-in on staging.desirableproperties.org: the Web3Auth config endpoint returns the staging ID (BL4DIH…), and production returns BKvRj4….
entries.intent: Staging and production each use their own Web3Auth project; a missing ID must fail loudly, never fall back to production's.

entries.title: Email key no longer kept in the code
entries.summary: The web app's setup and email-test scripts now read the Resend email key from the server environment instead of having it written into the code. The two keys that were in the code had already been switched off in Resend. No visible change on the site.
changes: create-env.sh writes RESEND_API_KEY from the environment and warns if it is missing
test-resend.js reads RESEND_API_KEY from the environment and stops if it is missing
The old keys stay in git history but no longer work
entries.intent: No secrets in the source of a public repo.

entries.title: Merging to main now deploys the site
entries.summary: The site and the book are deployed by production itself when a change is merged, instead of by GitHub logging into the old server. The old deploy jobs pointed at a server that is being retired, so they were removed. No visible change on the site.
changes: Removed the deploy-challenge-site and deploy-webapp workflows, which deployed to the retired server
The rail-sync workflow still syncs and commits; production publishes the book when that commit lands
Runtime files written on the server (loop state and logs, script cache) are ignored by git
entries.verify: After a merge to main, /var/log/pull-deploy/desirable-properties.log on production shows DEPLOY and OK for the new commit
entries.intent: Production deploys itself from main; GitHub holds no credential that reaches the server.

entries.title: Gov Hub links open the current draft, on interfacehub.net
entries.summary: Workgroup activity links now open the latest approved revision of each DP draft on Gov Hub instead of the original Revision 00. Every remaining hub.themetalayer.org link now points to interfacehub.net.
changes: Workgroup activity feed links drafts by ML number, so Gov Hub serves the current revision
hub.themetalayer.org and dev.hub.themetalayer.org replaced with interfacehub.net and dev.interfacehub.net across the site, book viewer, inscription data, welcome content, scripts and docs
Framing chapter link uses ML-Draft-026 instead of a pinned row id, so it follows new revisions
entries.intent: People who click through to patch a DP should land on the text the book shows, not an outdated revision.
entries.verify: Open a DP workgroup page and follow a draft link in its activity feed: it should open the current revision on interfacehub.net.

entries.title: Turn a Deepi conversation into a Canopi comment
entries.summary: Under Deepi's latest reply you can now draft a Canopi comment from that turn or from the whole thread. Deepi offers three versions (builder, steward, skeptic); you edit one, choose page comment, reply or quote, and post it under your own name, marked AI-assisted.
changes: Comment from this turn / from the whole thread buttons on Deepi's latest reply
Three perspective drafts, editable, with page / reply / quote targets
Posted as the signed-in person via their Canopi session, with aiAssist provenance
entries.intent: Help people bring what they worked out with Deepi into the community conversation, in their own words.

entries.title: Canopi chapter feeds cached and rate-capped
entries.summary: Activity and search read every chapter's Canopi feed on each call. Those reads are now cached for 60 seconds and at most 4 run at once, so the site no longer floods Canopi (about 2,600 requests in 4 minutes on 2026-09-25) and Canopi's sidebar stays fast.
changes: 60 s cache per chapter feed, shared by concurrent callers; failed reads are not cached
At most 4 Canopi feed requests in flight per server process
Test: npm run test:canopi-feed-cache
entries.intent: Stop DP from slowing Canopi for everyone (canopi#32).

entries.title: Estate changelog adopted
entries.summary: Desirable Properties now keeps a volunteer-readable change log that agents and meta-console can parse.
changes: Added changelog.json in estate-changelog/v1 form
CI fails PRs that change watched paths without a changelog entry
entries.intent: Start a human and machine changelog for challenge-site deploys
